content:
Dichotomies at the New Delhi World Book Fair cum Nakshatra 2024

As the 52nd year of the New Delhi World Book Fair comes to an end, its sister fair, Nakshatra also completes 16. A trade fair organized by the ITPO, Nakshatra is another Pragati Maidan grand event for Indian culture, businesses, & especially businesses built off of that culture: astrology, tarot, & all things con. This year, for the second time in a row, Nakshatra took place alongside the world book fair, its antithesis in mind & soul. The book fair stands for everything Nakshatra is an insult to, & yet there were aspects of faith, seeing & unseeing, to be found in both.
excerpt: A photo essay from the 52nd New Delhi World Book Fair and its unlikely neighbour, Nakshatra, the trade fair for astrology, tarot, and all things con, held side by side at Pragati Maidan. On the strange coexistence of faith and reason, superstition and literature, in one of the capital's great annual public spaces.

Illustrated by Mouli Sharma.
related.title: Ek Waqt ki Namaaz

related.excerpt: A photo essay from International Women's Day, 8th March 2026, at Jantar Mantar, where women from six to sixty gathered to protest the BJP government's neglect of women's safety and welfare, express solidarity with the women of Palestine and Iran, and raise demands for dignity, health, and work.
related.title: Bengal Remembers: Sengar, Epstein, and RG Kar's Legacy on International Women's Day in 2026

related.excerpt: A photo essay on autocratic politics and the suppression of thought, the first resource any authoritarian strips from a people is not dignity but the capacity for independent thinking. Photographs and text by Kanika Solanki, journalism student at the University of Delhi.
related.title: Dictate

related.excerpt: The Delhi Police on 28 September 2026 denied permission for a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for alleged abuse of authority and election irregularities, and manipulation of voter rolls through SIR on 2 October 2026 at Jantar Mantar. A delegation of prominent activists including Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, Nandita Narain and Prashant Bhushan visited the Parliament Street Police station for an hour long discussion regarding the same, but the efforts did not reap fruit, leading to questions about the culture of ‘police permitted’ protests being raised.
related.title: “Completely illogical”: Delegation seeking police permission for Jantar Mantar protest against Gyanesh Kumar on 2nd October denied, slam sycophantic culture
